Weather: - Heavy snowfall in the past 2 winters. Heavy rain fell on 15th May, impacting the snow. Snow deposits, from this flood, along the Beas River corridor in May Naggar Farm Weather: - 18/4/1894 to 11/5/1894= 1 mm over 24 days, so likely good conditions for snow ripening and melt - 12-16/5/1894= 59.4 mm, so rain to enhance melt or new snow at elevation - 17-21/5/1894= 0 mm, continued conditions for snow ripening and melt - 22/5/1894= 15 mm Flood: - 'Landslide-dam outburst flood' - Near outburst location (Dhassin) water height estimated (by Donald and King) to be c. 150 m, described as a 'hill of black water' - Downstream (Dobhi at Beas River confluence) flow characteristics given as: '450 yards (411 m) wide, 40 feet (12.2 m) high and running at 20 miles an hour (8.9 ms-1)'. This was proceeded by a violent tremor and strong winds Flood Event Sequence (Is some uncertainty in accounts): 1. Early afternoon 21 May a slope failure, including ice and snow, near Dhassin village (perhaps near Tundra Krung Hill) 2a. Around 1h later a second slope failure blocked Phojal Nalla, forming a lake. 1h later again the landslide dam was catastrophically breached, OR 2b. A single slope failure, in which debris entered a narrow ravine as a 'semi-liquid torrent of snow, ice, black earth and sand and water' (implies a debris flow), where is was temporarily checked, OR 2c. A landslide dam (unknown date), creating a lake which lasted a few weeks, and was then breached by snow avalanches on 21 May (perhaps more plausible and aligns with later contemporary accounts) 3. The flood starting at c. 1700, had seven distinct flood waves, at 15-20 minute intervals, each initially rising c. 150 m above the channel bed. In the intervening periods the channel discharge was negligible 4. Post- event high turbidity ('runs black' 'inky fluid')- certainly recorded in June 1894; dust clouds which continued for 4 months (implied continuing slope instability); Phojal Nalla landslide impoundment ('bund') was still partially intact and leaking in June 1894
